title: Fourier inversion
statement:
Let $S=\Spec k$ (with $V\cong\mathbf A^r_k$ of rank $r$, and let
$\iota':V\to V$ be the inverse of the addition). For every
constructible Weil complex $K$ on $V$ there are functorial
isomorphisms

$$
\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-r),
$$

and, with the same character,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong{\iota'}^*K(-r),
$$

where $(-r)$ is the $r$-fold Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist]
(exponent $r$: the relative dimension of the line, since the
compactly supported cohomology of the affine space
$\mathbf A^r_k$ carries the twist
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)$ – the Poincare dual of the constant
sheaf
– in the top-degree contribution of the fibre integral; for $r=1$
this is the single twist $(-1)$).
(*Source: Fourier–Deligne inversion with geometric Frobenius and
the normalization $[r]$ of [def-fd-transform]; the same-kernel
calculation as the same-character square; Laumon, *Transformation
de Fourier*, (1.2.2.1)–(1.2.2.3).*)

external.place: Laumon, *Transformation de Fourier*, (2.1.3), (2.5.6).*) By [lem-fd-kernel-composition] the composite $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is the kernel transform with kernel $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\ast\mathcal K_\psi$ and shift $[2r]$, and by [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] that kernel is $\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r]$.

proof.text: By [lem-fd-kernel-composition], the composite $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is the kernel transform with kernel $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\ast\mathcal K_\psi$ and shift $[2r]$. Applying [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] identifies this convolution kernel with $\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r]$ (and identifies the same-character convolution with the anti-diagonal kernel).

source.place: Opening paragraph, composition and convolution clauses

proof.text: Write $s_i:V\times_S V\to V$ for the projections. The diagonal $\Delta$ is closed: in affine coordinates its ideal is $(x_j-y_j)_{j=1}^r$. Thus it is proper, and [prop-functor-package] identifies $\Delta_!$ with $\Delta_*$. Since $s_1^*K$ is bounded constructible at field coefficients, [lem-weil-field-tor-amplitude] gives the finite Tor amplitude required by the package's projection formula. With $f=\Delta$, input $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and tensor factor $s_1^*K$, that formula gives $s_1^*K\otimes^L\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\cong\Delta_*K$, using $s_1\Delta=\operatorname{id}$. Compact-support composition then gives $s_{2,!}\Delta_*K\cong(s_2\Delta)_!K=K$. These are natural comparisons and are Weil-equivariant by the package's final clause.

For the twisted diagonal kernel, the same projection formula with input $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)$ gives $K(-r)[-2r][2r]=K(-r)$. For the second formula apply [lem-fd-kernel-composition] with both characters equal to $\psi$. Put $a=\iota'$ and $\gamma=(\operatorname{id},a):V\to V\times_S V$. The second formula of [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] is $\gamma_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r]$. The calculation of step 2, with $s_1\gamma=\operatorname{id}$ and $s_2\gamma=a$, gives $a_!K(-r)$ after shift cancellation. The Cartesian square with both maps to its lower-right corner equal to $a$ and the other two maps identities gives $a^*a_!\cong\operatorname{id}$ by the package's compact-support base change. Also $a_!a_!\cong\operatorname{id}$ by composition, since $a^2=\operatorname{id}$. Consequently $a^*\cong a_!$, and the result is $a^*K(-r)$. The twist is pulled back from the point, so projection formula identifies $a^*(K(-r))$ with $(a^*K)(-r)$. All comparisons are natural and Weil-equivariant.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S=\Spec k$ (with $V\cong\mathbf A^r_k$ of rank $r$, and let
$\iota':V\to V$ be the inverse of the addition). For every
constructible Weil complex $K$ on $V$ there are functorial
isomorphisms

$$
\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-r),
$$

and, with the same character,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong{\iota'}^*K(-r),
$$

where $(-r)$ is the $r$-fold Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist].

proof.text:
By [lem-fd-kernel-composition] the composite
$\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ is the kernel
transform with kernel $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\ast\mathcal K_\psi$ and shift
$[2r]$, and by [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] that kernel is
$\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r]$. The kernel transform with
kernel $\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is the identity functor:
$\Delta$ is a closed immersion, so the projection formula of
[prop-functor-package] gives
$s_1^*K\otimes^L\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\cong\Delta_*K$, and
$s_{2,!}\Delta_*={(s_2)}_\Delta{}_!=\operatorname{id}_V$ because
$s_2\circ\Delta=\operatorname{id}_V$. Hence

$$
\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)
\cong K(-r)[-2r][2r]=K(-r),
$$

the twist being that of [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] and the two shifts
cancelling. For the second formula the same computation with the
anti-diagonal kernel of [lem-fd-convolution-kernel] identifies
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ with the pullback along
$\iota'$ of the identity transform, whence ${\iota'}^*K(-r)$.
